title: SONiC won't build on a fresh Debian 10 - No such file or directory: '/proc/modules'
author: ncalad
body:
#### Description

I set up a fresh Debian 10 (buster) instance on Amazon EC2. After installing docker and installing the prerequisites, python, pip, jinja2 and j2cli and adding the user to the docker group, I encounter an error when running make all. 


#### Steps to reproduce the issue:
1. Stand up a fresh Debian 10 instance (in my case on EC2)
2. sudo modprobe overlay
3. Install docker 
4. Add user to docker group using sudo gpasswd -a ${USER} docker
5. git clone https://github.com/Azure/sonic-buildimage.git
6. make init
7. make configure PLATFORM=broadcom
8. make all

#### Describe the results you received:

Each test failed with this error:

name = 'eeprom'

def isModuleLoaded(name):
 with open('/proc/modules') as f:
E IOError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/proc/modules'

#### Describe the results you expected:


#### Output of `show version`:

```
(paste your output here)
```
#### Output of `show techsupport`:

```
(paste your output here or download and attach the file here )
```

#### Additional information you deem important (e.g. issue happens only occasionally):

<!--
     Also attach debug file produced by `sudo generate_dump`
-->

comments.author: lguohan
comments.body: not sure which test failed in your case. in general, the sonic image is built on top of ubuntu 20.04 or 18.04. Do not know if any one tried to build it on top of debian 10.

comments.author: ncalad
comments.body:
On Debian 10, many (possibly all) of the test cases failed with the same error for /proc/modules. Before the first failure, there were some statistics printed for test cases which passed successfully. 

Earlier I stood up a fresh Debian 10 instance inside a VM but ran into problems with a composed apt-get update command. It seemed to me that quotes would be needed around the arguments. Strangely, I did not have that issue when building on a fresh Debian 10 running on EC2. 

I tried to build on Ubuntu 20.04 and finally gave up on that. In hindsight, I think SONiC probably built but failed to run the tests suite. 

On Ubuntu, I had problems with python version issues as python2.7 seems to be embedded somewhere and I had problems with the make files trying to access /proc/cmdline from the docker side. 

This has not been a smooth build experience so far.  I am happy to go back to Ubuntu 20.04 and try to build again there. What do you recommend?

comments.author: qiluo-msft
comments.body:
You can find the build environment Ubuntu 16.04 recommended in https://github.com/Azure/sonic-buildimage/blob/master/README.md. My personal dev environment is Debian GNU/Linux 10 (buster), and it build and test fine.

You are talking about a unit test issue, not a build issue. Could you narrow down which repo and which test case is complaining? You may find corresponding build/test log in ./target/**/*.log. You can attach it if you find error message there.

comments.body: @Staphylo: Have you ever encountered build issues like this building the Arista platform modules? I have not. Maybe you can give some insight?

comments.author: Staphylo
comments.body:
@jleveque @ncalad, I will make the existence of this file optional when running the tests.
We did not consider builds in an environment where `CONFIG_MODULES` kconfig is not set.

comments.author: ncalad
comments.body: I encountered this problem on a fresh Ubuntu instance after installing the prerequisites in the build instructions. That seems to suggest that CONFIG_MODULES is not be set by default.

comments.author: Staphylo
comments.body:
@ncalad, what I meant here is that the kernel of your VM doesn't have support for dynamic kernel module loading (`CONFIG_MODULES` is a kernel config, not a sonic config)
This leads to the /proc/modules files not existing.

linkedPullRequests.title: [Arista] Update platform configurations and library
linkedPullRequests.author: Staphylo
linkedPullRequests.body:
Platform library changes
 - Fix the use of /proc/modules during testing, fixes #7463
 - Add `libsfp-eeprom.so` build to read/write xcvr eeproms in C
 - Add some more reboot-cause information
 - Write down temperature hw thresholds to the sensors
 - Report software thresholds through platform api
 - Writ `port_name sysfs` file of optoe`
 - Tests enhancements
 - Fix dependency issues for chassis provisioning

Platform configuration changes
 - Add `pcie.yaml` configuration for a few platforms
 - Mount `libsfp-eeprom.so` inside `pmon`
 - Fix `Arista-7050SX3-48C8` and `Arista-7050SX3-48YC8' platform and hwsku
 - Miscellaneous fixes
